name: yylex
prose: Flex-generated scanner of unbound's configuration lexer (configlexer.c; YY_DECL at 4828, slice 4857-5157 is inside its body, the rules table). On first use it initialises the scanner state, defaults yyin to stdin and yyout to stdout and creates the input buffer if none exists (4834-4856). It then repeatedly matches the longest input prefix with the generated DFA tables and runs the action of the matching rule through a switch on yy_act. The rule actions in the generated code either return a token number for a configuration keyword to the parser or just update lexer state (start conditions, line counters, buffer handling); at the end-of-buffer logic it either continues scanning, finishes the last match, or, at end of file, runs the end-of-file action and returns the scanner's end token (YY_NULL) through yyterminate() (7200-7263). An internal inconsistency calls YY_FATAL_ERROR (7269, 7291, 7360), which does not return normally. The function returns an int token value each time a rule returns, and otherwise keeps scanning.
note: [R:n/a] previously dropped as "not a function"; yylex is a real generated function (flex output), fixed from its structure. Partly read: the init code (4828-4856), the end-of-buffer handling (7200-7300 by labels) and the fatal-error calls; the rule action bodies in the slice (4857-5157) and the DFA tables were not read, so the individual tokens returned are not listed.

name: yyparse
prose: Bison-generated LALR parser of unbound's configuration grammar (configparser.c; function at 2807-8270, this slice 5406-5706 is inside its reduce actions). It takes no argument, keeps its state and value stacks on the C stack (initial depth YYINITDEPTH, growing them when full, and failing with YYNOMEM if they cannot grow), and starts by asking for a token (yychar = YYEMPTY, 2846-2850). Each cycle it pushes the state, reads a token with yylex when needed, looks up the action in the tables, and either shifts the token, accepts, or reduces by a rule (yyreduce, 3030) by running that rule's semantic action; the actions in this region call the configuration-building helpers (for example handlers that set fields of the config being parsed or log a parse error) and may use YYABORT or YYERROR in their action code. A syntax error calls yyerror with "syntax error", counts it, and tries to recover by popping states until one can shift the error token; at end of input during recovery it aborts (8118-8214). It ends at yyreturnlab, which discards the lookahead symbol and the stacks, frees a heap-grown stack if any, and returns yyresult (8245-8269): 0 for accept (8221), 1 for abort (8229), and 2 for memory exhaustion (8238).
note: [R:n/a] no reviewer remarks recorded. This is one of three records for the same function (slices 5406-5706, 6991-7244, 8008-8268). Partly read: the head (2807-2860), the error and return labels (8118-8270) and the label/goto map of the skeleton; the individual reduce actions (3030-8112, the part in this slice) were not read, so the specific helper calls are named only generally.

name: yyparse
prose: Bison-generated LALR parser of unbound's configuration grammar (configparser.c; function at 2807-8270, this slice 8008-8268 covers the last reduce actions and the tail). It takes no argument, keeps its state and value stacks on the C stack (initial depth YYINITDEPTH, growing them when full, and failing with YYNOMEM if they cannot grow), and starts by asking for a token (yychar = YYEMPTY, 2846-2850). Each cycle it pushes the state, reads a token with yylex when needed, looks up the action in the tables, and either shifts the token, accepts, or reduces by a rule (yyreduce, 3030) by running that rule's semantic action and then pushing the left-hand-side state (goto yynewstate at 8112). A syntax error is counted and reported with yyerror; with an error status of 3 an unusable lookahead is discarded and end of input aborts (8123-8146), then states are popped until one accepts the error token and, when the stack is empty, the parse aborts (8175-8214). The label yyacceptlab sets yyresult to 0, yyabortlab to 1 and yyexhaustedlab to 2, and all end at yyreturnlab, which destroys the lookahead if it is still held, pops all stack entries, frees a heap-grown stack and returns yyresult (8220-8269).
note: [R:n/a] no reviewer remarks recorded. Tail read: 8112-8270 line by line, plus the head (2807-2860); the last reduce actions in this slice (8008-8112) were not read.

name: change_rrsig_rrset
prose: Converts an RRSIG-only rrset of a parsed message into a data rrset of type datatype, or splits the signatures into a new rrset (unbound msgparse.c:397-446; slice cut the head); it returns the data rrset or NULL on allocation failure. It first computes the hash of the data rrset (402-403). If hasother is set it creates a new rrset in the given section with new_rrset (returning NULL on failure), increments the section's rrset counter, moves the RRSIGs over with moveover_rrsigs (returning NULL on failure) and returns the new rrset (406-424). If hasother is 0 it reuses sigset itself: it removes it from its hash bucket, reinserts it under the new hash, calls change_section, sets the type and flags, and turns its records into signatures by adding rr_count to rrsig_count, linking the record list behind any existing signature list and clearing rr_first and rr_last (427-444). change_section returns at once without moving the rrset or changing the section counters when section already equals the rrset's section (msgparse.c:292-293), so in that case only the other fields change. It returns the rrset at 445.
note: [R:right] reviewer: for hasother==0 the postcondition claims a move/count update when section equals sigset->section, but change_section returns early - right (change_section at msgparse.c:292-293, called at 433). Slice cut the head; function read in full, plus change_section; new_rrset, moveover_rrsigs and msgparse_bucket_remove not read.

name: event_add
prose: Registers an event with the minimal libevent-like event base of unbound (mini_event.c:292-325; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 if the descriptor is out of range. If the event is already added it first removes it with event_del (294-295), so that removal has happened even when the function then returns -1. It returns -1 without adding anything if the descriptor is set and not below the base's capfd (296-297); in that case the event is left removed and not added. For a read or write event with a valid descriptor it records the event in the descriptor table, sets the read and/or write bits and the content bit, clears the ready bit and raises maxfd if needed (298-310). With a timeout argument and an EV_TIMEOUT event it computes the absolute timeout from the base time plus tv (with microsecond carry) and inserts the event into the timer tree (311-322). It then sets ev->added to 1 and returns 0 (323-324).
note: [R:right] reviewer: event_add calls event_del before the capfd check, so the -1 path can change state; the annotation says no state change - right (294-297). Slice cut the head; function read in full; event_del not read.

name: http_process_chunk_header
prose: Processes one line of an HTTP chunked-transfer header or trailer from the comm point's buffer (netevent.c:4907-4960; slice cut the head); it returns 0, 1 or 2. It returns 1 at once if no complete header line is available (4909-4910). In trailer mode (http_in_chunk_headers == 3): an empty line when tcp_byte_count is 0 empties the buffer, calls the callback with NETEVENT_DONE and returns 2 (4914-4922); an empty line otherwise switches back to chunk-header mode (1), moves the buffer content over and returns 1 (4924-4930); a non-empty trailer line returns 1 (4933). In chunk-size mode (http_in_chunk_headers == 1) it parses the line with strtol in base 16; it returns 0 if no digit was consumed, errno is set, or the value is negative, and the check is only on the start of the line, so trailing characters after the hexadecimal digits (such as chunk extensions or junk) are accepted (4936-4946). Otherwise it stores the chunk size in tcp_byte_count, leaves header mode, moves the buffer content over, flips the buffer, switches to trailer mode when the size is 0, and returns 1 (4947-4956). For any other mode it returns 1 (4959).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the code accepts trailing non-hex junk in the chunk size, while the annotation said invalid hex returns 0 - right (4941-4942 test only end==line, errno and negativity). Slice cut the head; function read in full; http_header_line and http_moveover_buffer not read.

name: autr_process_prime
prose: Processes a fetched DNSKEY rrset for an RFC 5011 auto-trust anchor (unbound autotrust.c:2169-2280; slice cut the head); it returns 1 normally and 0 when the trust point was removed, revoked, or its next probe could not be set. On entry it expects tp->lock held. A revoked trust point is unlocked and 0 is returned (2180-2186). It records the query time, reassembles the keys after hold-down expiry and returns 1 when that allocation fails (2189-2201). Without a DNSKEY rrset it returns 1 (2203-2210). It checks for revoked keys and, if changed, reassembles (return 1 on failure) and, when no DS and no DNSKEY rrset remain, records the success time, calls autr_tp_remove and returns 0 (2212-2225). If the DNSKEY set does not verify it increments query_failed and writes the file when there was an earlier success, and returns 1 (2228-2237). Otherwise it records success, resets query_failed, calls update_events and do_statetable (each failing with an out-of-memory log and return 1), cleans up keys, and returns 0 if set_next_probe fails (2239-2264); then it writes the file and, if changed, reassembles (return 1 on failure) and removes the trust point with autr_tp_remove and returns 0 when no DS and no DNSKEY rrset remain (2265-2276), else returns 1 (2279). autr_tp_remove unlocks tp->lock, deletes the trust point from the anchor tree and frees it only if it was still in the tree; if another thread already deleted it nothing is freed here (autotrust.c:2142-2163).
note: [R:right] reviewer: return 0 via autr_tp_remove does not always free tp; del_tp may be NULL - right (autotrust.c:2146 and 2156-2162, only freed when del_tp is non-NULL). Slice cut the head; function read in full, plus autr_tp_remove; the update, verify and statetable helpers not read.

name: anchors_swap_tree
prose: Swaps the trust anchor tree and the auto-trust probe tree between two validator anchor sets (val_anchor.c:1386-1403); the packet name anchors_swap does not exist. It returns without doing anything if either anchors or data is NULL (1392-1393). Otherwise it saves anchors->tree and anchors->autr->probe, assigns data's tree and probe to anchors, and gives the saved ones to data (1395-1402), the probe structure being copied by value. It takes no locks, so the caller must ensure exclusive access, and both autr pointers must be non-NULL because they are dereferenced.
note: [R:n/a] still-rejected only because "anchors_swap" is not the name in the file; the real function is anchors_swap_tree (val_anchor.c:1386-1403, read in full).

name: validate_nameerror_response
prose: Validates a NXDOMAIN reply with NSEC or NSEC3 proofs (unbound validator.c:1271-1372; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and reports through chase_reply->security, *rcode and *suspend. It clears *suspend and scans the authority rrsets: an NSEC that proves the name does not exist sets has_valid_nsec, one with the best closest encloser that proves no covering wildcard sets has_valid_wnsec (the flag may be cleared again by a later NSEC of the same depth), and an NSEC proving an insecure delegation sets the reply to sec_status_insecure and returns at once; an NSEC3 only marks nsec3s_seen (1287-1313). If either NSEC proof is missing and NSEC3 records were seen, it runs the NSEC3 proof: an unchecked result sets *suspend and returns, any other result that is not secure keeps that security value in chase_reply->security and returns without trying the NODATA fallback, and a secure result sets both has_valid flags (1315-1334). If the name-error proof is missing, or the wildcard proof is missing, it runs validate_nodata_response and returns after suspend; if that leaves the reply secure it changes *rcode to NOERROR, otherwise it marks the reply bogus with the DNSSEC-bogus reason (1337-1366). If both proofs hold it sets the reply secure (1370-1371).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: claims a bogus NSEC3 name-error result sets security immediately, while the code falls through to the NODATA fallback and may set secure - wrong: after nsec3_prove_nameerror, a result that is neither unchecked nor secure goes to the return at validator.c:1326-1330 with chase_reply->security already holding that result; only a secure result continues, and then both has_valid flags are set so the fallbacks at 1337 and 1353 are not run. Slice cut the head; function read in full; the NSEC helpers and validate_nodata_response not read.

name: processFindKey
prose: Validator step that finds the key needed to validate the reply (unbound validator.c:2026-2185; slice cut the head); it returns 1 when validation should continue in the current invocation (the state in vq->state decides what runs next) and 0 when it is waiting for a sub-query or has finished the event, or the result of val_error on an error. If the key entry is a null key (an earlier DNSKEY lookup failed with retry) it generates a DNSKEY sub-query for the DS owner name and returns 0, or val_error if generating the request fails; this return 0 does not set vq->state (2040-2048). It picks the target key name from the signer name (or the query name) and compares it with the current key entry name; equal names set vq->state to VAL_VALIDATE_STATE and return 1 (2050-2063). If the target equals the last empty-DS name it marks the reply bogus, sets VAL_FINISHED_STATE and returns 1; otherwise that name becomes the current name (2065-2081). If the target is not below the current name it marks the reply bogus, sets VAL_FINISHED_STATE and returns 1 (2088-2093). It strips labels to find the next name (2095-2102). If a DS rrset exists for a different name than the current key it sends a DNSKEY request for it and returns 0 (2112-2121). If no DS rrset exists for the next name it processes a suspended sub-query DS reply or a cached DS reply with process_ds_response (suspension sets up a timer in VAL_FINDKEY_STATE and returns 0, or val_error if the timer fails; a processed cached reply returns 1) and otherwise sends a DS request and returns 0 (2123-2173). Otherwise it sends the DNSKEY request for the DS name and returns 0 (2177-2184).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the DNSKEY sub-query return 0 does not set vq->state to VAL_FINDKEY_STATE - right (2047, 2120 and 2184 return 0 without touching vq->state; only validate_suspend_setup_timer is given VAL_FINDKEY_STATE at 2145, 2161). Slice cut the head; function read in full; generate_request, process_ds_response and val_find_DS not read.

name: process_prime_response
prose: Handles the reply to the DNSKEY priming query for the current trust anchor (unbound validator.c:3456-3518; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and sets vq->state and vq->key_entry. It looks up the trust anchor (the anchor lock is held on success); if there is none it sets VAL_INIT_STATE, or VAL_VALIDATE_STATE when no anchor name was set, clears the anchor name and returns (3462-3471). For a NOERROR reply it finds the DNSKEY rrset in the answer section (3475-3479). For an auto-trust anchor it calls autr_process_prime and, if that returns 0, sets VAL_INIT_STATE, clears the anchor name and returns without unlocking here (3481-3488). It then builds the key entry with primeResponseToKE and unlocks the anchor (3490-3492). Only if a key entry exists: a bad entry with restarts left blacklists the origin, clears the error info, counts the restart, resets the entry and state to VAL_INIT_STATE and returns; otherwise it clears chain_blacklist, adds error info (origin and trust anchor name) and caches the entry (3493-3510). With no key entry the blacklist clearing and the error info are skipped. Finally, if the key entry is missing, null or bad, the state becomes VAL_VALIDATE_STATE (3513-3516).
note: [R:right] reviewer: for a NULL key_entry the code skips the chain_blacklist clear and errinf; the annotation says they happen - right (3504-3506 are inside if(vq->key_entry), 3493). Slice cut the head; function read in full; primeResponseToKE and the key cache helpers not read.

name: sentinel_get_keytag
prose: Parses the key tag out of a root-sentinel query label (unbound validator.c:593-608; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. It allocates a zeroed buffer of SENTINEL_KEYTAG_LEN+1 bytes, returning 0 if that fails (596-598). It copies SENTINEL_KEYTAG_LEN bytes from start into it (always reading that many bytes), terminates it, stores strtol(buffer, &e, 10) cast to uint16_t into *keytag, and returns 0 if e is NULL or does not point at the terminating NUL (599-605); so non-digit characters, a leading sign or blank followed by a non-digit, and an input with no digits (for example only blanks) return 0, while an input containing a NUL early, or leading white space followed by digits that fill the string, may return 1. The buffer is freed on all paths and 1 is returned otherwise (606-607). *keytag is written before the check, so it holds a value even on the failure return.
note: [R:right] reviewer: whitespace-only input returns 0, not 1: strtol leaves endptr at the start when no conversion happens - right (601-602: e stays at the start of the blank buffer, so *e is not NUL). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: kernel_set_device
prose: Sends a WireGuard device configuration to the FreeBSD kernel (wireguard-tools ipc-freebsd.h:250-362); the packet name wg_set_device does not exist, the function is kernel_set_device. It copies the interface name, builds an nvlist for the device, counts the peers and allocates an array of peer nvlists, and adds the private key, listen port, fwmark (as "user-cookie") and replace-peers flag when the corresponding flags are set (258-278). For each peer it creates an nvlist, counts allowed IPs, adds the public key, optional preshared key, keepalive interval, endpoint (for AF_INET and AF_INET6 only), replace-allowedips and remove flags, and builds an nvlist for each allowed IP with its flags, cidr and address; the allowed-ips array is attached and the temporary nvlists freed when there is at least one (280-326). A failure while building a peer jumps to err_peer, which sets ret from errno, frees the allowed-IP nvlists and the peer nvlist and continues at err (328-335). After the loop it attaches the peers array and frees the peer nvlists (337-343), packs the device nvlist (a NULL result goes to err), frees the device nvlist, gets a datagram socket and returns -errno if that fails, and otherwise returns the result of ioctl(s, SIOCSWG, &wgd), which is 0 on success and -1 on failure, not an errno value (344-352). The packed buffer wgd.wgd_data is not freed in this function on either of those returns. At err it sets ret to -errno if it was 0, frees the peer nvlists and the device nvlist and returns ret (354-361).
note: [R:n/a] still-rejected only because "wg_set_device" is not a name in the file; fixed under the real name kernel_set_device (read in full, 250-362). nvlist_*, get_dgram_socket and the ioctl not read.

name: hostapd_config_read_eap_user
prose: Reads the hostapd EAP user database file into conf->eap_user (hostapd config_file.c:251-578; the packet name hostapd_config_read_eap_user_file does not exist). It returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. If fname starts with "sqlite:" it stores a copy of the rest in conf->eap_user_sqlite and returns 0 (or returns -1 when SQLite support is not built in) without reading any file (259-268); a file that cannot be opened returns -1 (271-275). It reads the file line by line, skipping comment lines and empty lines and stripping the newline (278-292). A "radius_accept_attr=" line after a user entry parses an attribute and appends it to that user's list, or fails (295-312). Any other line must start with '"' (a user name, up to the closing quote) or '*' (wildcard); otherwise the whole read fails (318-321). For each user it allocates an entry (allocation failure fails), parses the method list, the password or other fields and the flags, and appends it to a local list that is only installed at the end (324-558, parse errors jumping to failed). On failure it frees the current entry, sets ret to -1 and stops (561-565). After the loop it closes the file; on success it frees the previous conf->eap_user list and installs the new list, otherwise it frees the new list (568-575), and returns ret (577).
note: [R:n/a] still-rejected only for the wrong name; the real function is hostapd_config_read_eap_user (config_file.c:251-578), fixed under that name. Partly read: head (251-345) and tail (555-578), plus a scan of the goto lines; the per-line parsing of methods, passwords and the flag fields (346-554) was not read.

name: hostapd_config_fill
prose: Applies one "name=value" line of a hostapd configuration file to conf and bss (hostapd config_file.c:2439-5110; slice cut the head); buf holds the option name, pos the value and line the line number used in messages. It is a single long if/else chain on os_strcmp(buf, name). Each branch parses pos for its option and stores the result in the configuration (atoi, a string copy with os_strdup or os_strlcpy, a get_u16/parse helper, a lookup table); most branches return 1 after logging an error when the value is invalid, and the function returns 0 at its end when the matched branch finished normally (5109). An unknown option logs "unknown configuration item" and returns 1 (5102-5106). A few branches return other values: ctrl_interface_group returns 0 at once when the group name is found by getgrnam (3293-3299) and 1 when it is neither a known group nor a number (3303-3307); acs_chan_bias returns -1 when parsing fails (3434-3437). In the region of the slice, rxkh_file replaces the stored file name, returns 1 if os_strdup fails, but when hostapd_config_read_rxkh_file fails it only logs the error and does not return 1 (3261-3275), so the function then returns 0; ctrl_interface frees the old string and stores os_strdup(pos) without checking the copy (3284-3286).
note: [R:right] reviewer: rxkh_file read failure is logged but not returned as 1; some os_strdup allocation failures are unchecked - right (3269-3275 has no return in the failure branch, 3286 stores the strdup unchecked). Partly read: head (2439-2470), the region 3259-3312, 3430-3440 and the tail (5090-5110), plus a grep of the return statements; the bodies of the other roughly two hundred option branches (2470-3258, 3312-5090) were not read.

name: hostapd_ctrl_iface_eapol_rx
prose: Handles the EAPOL_RX control command of hostapd (ctrl_iface.c:1770-1805; the packet name is wrong in its qualifier only, the slice cut the head): the command text is "<MAC> <hex>". It logs the command, parses the MAC address with hwaddr_aton2 and returns -1 if that fails (1779-1782), skips spaces, and returns -1 if the remaining hex text has an odd length (1784-1789). It allocates len/2 bytes (-1 if that fails), converts the hex text with hexstr2bin (freeing the buffer and returning -1 if it is invalid), calls ieee802_1x_receive(hapd, src, buf, len, FRAME_ENCRYPTION_UNKNOWN), frees the buffer and returns 0 (1792-1804).

name: hostapd_cli_reconnect
prose: Reconnects hostapd_cli to the control interface ifname (hostapd_cli.c:155-183; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It first closes the current connection (159). A NULL ifname returns -1 (161-162). It stores a copy of ifname in the global ctrl_ifname (freeing the old name first, so the old name is lost even if the copy fails) and returns -1 if the copy fails (164-168). It opens a connection with hostapd_cli_open_connection into ctrl_conn and returns -1 if that fails (170-172). If the client is neither interactive nor running an action file it returns 0 without attaching (173-174). Otherwise it attaches with wpa_ctrl_attach: on success it sets hostapd_cli_attached, registers the event handler and calls update_stations; on failure it prints a warning; either way it returns 0 (175-182).

Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: main
prose: Entry point of the hs20 OSU client (osu_client.c:3228-3473; slice cut the head). It initialises the context (return -1 on failure, 3241-3242), parses options (d, f, h, K, N, o, O, q, r, s, S, t, T, w, x) with getopt, where -h or an unknown option prints usage and calls exit(0) (3244-3297), and exits with 0 after usage when there is no command argument (3299-3302). It opens the debug file, makes stdout line buffered, removes an old result file, runs check_workarounds and then dispatches on the command name: to_tnds, to_tnds2, from_tnds, sub_rem, pol_upd, prov, sim_prov, dl_osu_ca, dl_polupd_ca, dl_aaa_ca, osu_select, signup, set_pps, get_fqdn, oma_dm_prov, oma_dm_sim_prov and the others in the tail (3316-3420). Commands that need arguments check argc - optind against a minimum and call usage and exit(0) when too few are given; the get_fqdn check is "argc - optind < 1", which cannot be true at that point (the earlier test already requires one argument), so get_fqdn with no operand does not call usage but calls cmd_get_fqdn with argv[optind + 1], which is NULL (3400-3405). oma_dm_sim_prov returns -1 from main after writing a summary when the command result is negative (3419-3421). Several commands set ret from their command function; the function returns ret at 3473.

Partly read: the head, option loop labels and the command dispatch (3228-3420); the tail commands after 3420 and the option bodies (3248-3291) were only scanned, and the cmd_* functions were not read.

name: hostapd_set_security_params
prose: Derives the cipher and security-policy fields of a BSS configuration from its wpa, 802.1X, WEP and OSEN settings (ap_config.c:1607-1685; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. With CONFIG_WEP and no individual WEP key length it sets broadcast_key_idx_min to 0 (1610-1615). If WPA2 is enabled and rsn_pairwise is 0 it copies wpa_pairwise into it (1618-1619). It sets wpa_group to group_cipher when that is set, otherwise to the cipher chosen by wpa_select_ap_group_cipher, and, unless the rekey interval was set explicitly, sets wpa_group_rekey to 600 for TKIP or 86400 otherwise (1620-1628). With full_config it points the RADIUS auth and accounting server at the first configured entries (1630-1633). It then picks the security policy: WPA with 802.1X gives SECURITY_WPA and WPA without it SECURITY_WPA_PSK (1635-1638); 802.1X alone gives SECURITY_IEEE_802_1X, sets the WEP default length, sets wpa_group, wpa_pairwise and rsn_pairwise to a cipher that depends on the WEP key length only when full_config is set (otherwise to WPA_CIPHER_NONE), and sets wpa_key_mgmt only when full_config is set (1639-1658); static WEP keys give SECURITY_STATIC_WEP, set the three ciphers from the key length and, with full_config, the key management (1660-1669); OSEN sets SECURITY_OSEN with CCMP as group and rsn pairwise cipher and pairwise 0 (1671-1675); otherwise it sets SECURITY_PLAINTEXT and, only when full_config is set, sets the three ciphers and wpa_key_mgmt to none (1676-1684).

name: hostapd_dfs_background_start_channel_switch
prose: Reacts to a radar detection when background radar detection (a dedicated radar chain) may be used (dfs.c:1319-1362; slice cut the head); it returns -1, 0 or the result of hostapd_dfs_start_channel_switch_background. It returns -1 if background radar detection is not in use (1322-1323). It returns 0 without changing anything if a channel switch announcement is already in progress (1331-1332). If the radar was reported on the background chain itself (hostapd_dfs_is_background_event) it updates the background chain with a new random channel and returns 0 (1334-1342). Otherwise it returns -1 if the background chain has no channel (1349-1350); if background CAC is still running it sets radar_background.temp_ch to 1 and returns -1 so that CAC is done on the main chain, which is a state change (1352-1358). Otherwise it returns the result of hostapd_dfs_start_channel_switch_background(iface) (1361).
note: [R:right] reviewer: claims no side effects for the background CAC case but it sets temp_ch=1 - right (1357). Slice cut the head; function read in full; the helper functions not read.

name: hostapd_handle_dfs
prose: Decides whether CAC (channel availability check) is needed on the configured channel and starts it (dfs.c:829-944; slice cut the head); it returns 1 when no DFS action is required or the check can be skipped or the background chain is used, 0 when CAC is running (or no valid channel was found), and -1 on failure. It returns 1 immediately for a 6 GHz frequency or when no current_mode is known (834-845). It clears cac_started and, in a loop, gets the start channel index (-1 returns -1), the number of used channels and the CAC time (849-861); if no channel needs radar detection it returns 1 (864-869), if all required channels are already available it returns 1 and skips CAC (872-877), and if some are unavailable it calls dfs_set_valid_channel: when that fails it sets the interface state to HAPD_IFACE_DFS and returns 0, otherwise it repeats the loop (880-890). After the loop it sets the DFS state, logs the CAC start and calls hostapd_start_dfs_cac, returning -1 if that fails (893-918). When a background radar chain is in use it records the current channel in radar_background, then selects a random channel on the dedicated chain with dfs_set_valid_channel (returning its negative result), sets radar_background.temp_ch to 1 and returns 1; this selection happens after the CAC start, not before (920-940). Otherwise it returns 0 (943).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the background branch starts CAC before selecting the temp channel; the annotation says CAC is started on the temporary channel - right (hostapd_start_dfs_cac at 905-913 runs before dfs_set_valid_channel at 935). Slice cut the head; function read in full; the dfs_* helpers not read.

name: hostapd_acs_channel_selected
prose: Applies the channel chosen by the driver's ACS (automatic channel selection) to the configuration (drv_callbacks.c:1371-1509; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. With CONFIG_IEEE80211BE and a link id it switches to that link's BSS and returns if there is none (1378-1387). It returns without changes if a channel is already configured (1390-1393). It sets iface->freq to the selected primary frequency (1396), which stays set even when later checks fail. If there is no current mode it looks for the hardware mode matching acs_res->hw_mode (and containing the frequency) and, if none is found, logs "bad hw_mode", sets err and goes to out (1398-1420); a zero primary frequency or a frequency for which no channel is found also set err and go to out, before iconf->channel is touched (1423-1440). Only after those checks does it set iconf->channel and acs, derive the secondary channel offset from sec_freq (a secondary equal to the primary sets err and goes to out after channel and acs were already set, 1442-1455) and store the EDMG channel (1457). For VHT or HE it sets segment indices and channel width from ch_width 40, 80 or 160 (1459-1489), with CONFIG_IEEE80211BE it also handles a 320 MHz width and the puncture bitmap (1491-1501). At out it calls hostapd_acs_completed(hapd->iface, err) and only logs a warning if that returns nonzero (1503-1508).
note: [R:right] reviewer: claims iconf fields are set on invalid hw_mode/pri_freq/primary-channel paths, but the code jumps to out before setting them - right (1419, 1428, 1439 precede 1442-1443). Slice cut the head; function read in full; hostapd_acs_completed and the hw_* helpers not read.

name: hostapd_notif_update_dh_ie
prose: Handles a request from the driver to update the OWE (Diffie-Hellman) information element of a peer (drv_callbacks.c:2282-2360; slice cut the head); it returns -1 for invalid arguments and 0 otherwise, with errors reported to the driver. It returns -1 if hapd or its wpa_auth is missing or peer is NULL (2290-2297). If OWE is not in the key management, or the elements cannot be parsed, or owe_validate_request returns a non-success status, it goes to err (2298-2313). It finds or adds the station: for an existing one it stops the session timeout and accounting and sets the inactivity timeout to STA_NULLFUNC; adding a new one that fails goes to err (2315-2331). It clears the WPS flags and, only when CONFIG_IEEE80211BE is compiled in and link_addr is non-NULL, fills in the station's MLD information (2332-2346). It then calls owe_process_rsn_ie and frees the station if that returns a non-success status, and returns 0 (2349-2355). The err label tells the driver the failure status through hostapd_drv_update_dh_ie (using link_addr when it is non-NULL, otherwise peer) and returns 0 (2356-2359).
note: [R:right] reviewer: MLD link info is set only under CONFIG_IEEE80211BE, not whenever link_addr is non-NULL - right (2334-2346). Slice cut the head; function read in full; owe_* and ap_sta_* helpers not read.

name: hostapd_notif_assoc
prose: Handles a driver association or reassociation event for station addr (drv_callbacks.c:251-910; slice cut the head). The return value is mixed: -1 on rejected or failed association (after cleanup), 0 when the event is ignored or completed, and, in some inner branches, positive WLAN_STATUS_* codes. It returns -1 if addr is NULL (272-283) and 0 if addr is a multicast, zero or the AP's own address (285-294). It parses the request elements (parse failure returns -1) and selects the WPS, RSN, WPA or OSEN element if any (302-331). It finds the existing station (stopping its session timeout and accounting) or adds a new one; if adding fails it disassociates the address and returns -1 (333-349). If WPA is enabled and an SA query is needed it sends an association response with status ASSOC_REJECTED_TEMPORARILY and a comeback time and returns 0 (352-357). The middle part (360-900) validates the WPA/RSN/OSEN/WPS elements, MBO and other options and sets up the station; several of its early exits are "goto fail" (380, 393, 412, 485, 593, 612, 627, 644, 758, 805, 832, 866) and others return WLAN_STATUS_INVALID_IE or WLAN_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE directly (665, 675, 679, 692, 702, 713, 720, 728) or 0 (771, 801). A normal completion returns 0 (900). The fail label sends an association response with the status when status is not negative, disassociates the station, frees it with ap_free_sta and returns -1, not 0 (902-909).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: the common fail path returns 0 after sending the response and freeing the STA, not -1 - wrong: the fail label ends with `return -1` (909). Partly read: head and early part (251-360), the OSEN part (655-690) and the tail (895-910); the long middle (360-655 and 690-895: WPA validation, MBO, HT/VHT/HE handling, accounting, P2P) was not read, only scanned for returns and gotos.

name: hostapd_get_eap_user
prose: Finds the EAP user entry for an identity (eap_user_db.c:232-290; the packet name get_eap_user does not exist). With WPS enabled, an identity equal to the WSC enrollee identity returns a static entry (rewritten on each call) whose only method is WSC, and one equal to the WSC registrar identity returns a static entry with the WSC method and the AP PIN as password (239-258). Otherwise it scans the configured user list from conf->eap_user: for phase 1 (phase2 == 0) an entry with a NULL identity is taken as a match (261-265); an entry of the right phase with a wildcard prefix matches when identity_len is at least the stored length and the stored identity is a prefix of identity (267-273); an entry of the right phase whose identity has the same length and bytes matches (275-278). The first match ends the scan. If nothing matched and an SQLite user database is configured it returns the result of eap_user_sqlite_get (283-286); otherwise it returns the match found or NULL (289).
note: [R:n/a] previously dropped as the wrong name; the function exists (hostapd_get_eap_user at eap_user_db.c:232-290) and is fixed. Read in full; eap_server_get_type and eap_user_sqlite_get not read.

name: handle_auth_sae
prose: Handles a received SAE authentication frame for station sta (ieee802_11.c:1306-1639; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and sends the reply itself. resp starts as WLAN_STATUS_SUCCESS (1310). With the reflection-attack test option and transaction 1, or the commit-override option and transaction 1, it sends the prepared reply and goes to remove_sta (1322-1343). If there is no SAE state yet, only transaction 1 with an acceptable status is allowed, otherwise resp is UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE and it replies; the state is allocated (failure goes to remove_sta) and set to SAE_NOTHING (1345-1360). Transaction 1 (commit) handling (1360-1546) checks the anti-clogging token and rejected groups, can reply with an anti-clogging request, and calls sae_sm_step; transaction 2 (confirm) goes to remove_sta if the status is not success, replies UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE if the confirm is too short, silently returns for an unexpected confirm in the ACCEPTED state, replies CHALLENGE_FAIL if sae_check_confirm fails, then calls sae_sm_step (1547-1589); any other transaction number goes to remove_sta if the status is not success, else resp becomes UNKNOWN_AUTH_TRANSACTION (1590-1598). At reply, if the station was not removed and resp is not success, it sends the failure status to the driver and sends an auth reply, clearing a stored password identifier for a rejected first commit (1601-1626). At remove_sta it removes a station that was added unassociated when resp or the frame status was not success (1628-1637) and frees the data buffer (1638).
note: [R:n/a] the reviewer's remark (a SAE_NOTHING state with a non-1 transaction returns SUCCESS after a log, without a state transition) concerns the state machine step called from here (sae_sm_step), which was not read, so it is neither confirmed nor refuted. Partly read: head (1306-1360), the confirm and unknown-transaction branches (1496-1520, 1546-1600) and the tail (1601-1639); the transaction-1 branch (1360-1546) was scanned only by goto/return lines (goto reply at 1351, 1388, 1395, 1512, 1516, 1542; remove_sta at 1406, 1420, 1436, 1440, 1486, 1496, 1508; return at 1426, 1445).

name: handle_auth
prose: Processes a received IEEE 802.11 Authentication management frame at the AP (ieee802_11.c:2870-3336; the packet slice 1545-1807 does not contain this function, it covers the SAE helpers before it); it returns nothing and replies through send_auth_reply. It returns without a reply when the frame is shorter than the header plus the auth body (2889-2893) or when the testing option drops it by probability (2896-2902). After the header checks (2905-3227, in the part that was scanned only by gotos and returns: a number of failures go to the fail label with a status in resp, and silent returns happen for ignored, queued or duplicate frames, at 3082, 3096, 3113, 3121, 3139), it dispatches on the authentication algorithm (3229): open system marks the station authenticated and calls mlme_authenticate_indication (3230-3238); shared key calls auth_shared_key, sets the algorithm and, for transaction 1 with a stored challenge, adds the challenge element to the reply (3241-3256); FT initialises the WPA state machine (failure goes to fail) and calls wpa_ft_process_auth, then returns (3260-3277); SAE initialises the state machine in mesh mode (failure goes to fail) and calls handle_auth_sae, which sends its own reply, then returns (3280-3298); FILS and PASN call their handlers and return (3301-3313). Paths that reach fail, or leave the switch for open or shared key, send an auth reply with resp and the optional response elements, with the transaction number plus 1 except for SAE, and remove a station that was added unassociated if resp or the send result is not success (3317-3335). The SAE-specific reply statuses such as CHALLENGE_FAIL and FINITE_CYCLIC_GROUP_NOT_SUPPORTED are produced in handle_auth_sae, not in this function.
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: omits the SAE CHALLENGE_FAIL and FINITE_CYCLIC_GROUP_NOT_SUPPORTED reply statuses that the code sends - not applicable to handle_auth: those statuses are set in handle_auth_sae (ieee802_11.c:1583 and 1608), which the reviewer saw in the slice; handle_auth only calls it (3296-3298) and returns. Partly read: the head (2870-2905) and the dispatch and tail (3226-3336); the header checks and the station setup (2905-3226) were scanned only by goto and return lines. The real function is outside the packet slice.

name: ieee80211_ml_process_link
prose: Processes one non-association link of an MLO (multi-link) association request on the AP (ieee802_11.c:4501-4622; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 when the final status is not success. It parses the link's elements; a parse failure sets status UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE and goes to out (4516-4520). If a station with the origin address already exists on this link BSS it fails with UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE (4522-4528); otherwise it adds one with ap_sta_add, and if that fails sets AP_UNABLE_TO_HANDLE_NEW_STA and goes to out (4530-4535). It defragments the Basic Multi-Link element; if that fails it goes to out with status still SUCCESS, which returns 0 without having completed the link processing (4537-4539). It parses the link-specific association request, runs __check_assoc_ies, copies the MLD and flag information and, unless offloaded, takes the AID from the origin station (a zero AID fails) and marks it used, shares the WPA state machine and sets flags (4541-4601), and unless offloaded calls add_associated_sta, whose failure sets AP_UNABLE_TO_HANDLE_NEW_STA (4605-4606). At out it frees the buffer, stores the status in link->status, builds the link's association response unless offloaded, and, when the status is not success, frees the new station (if any) and returns -1, else returns 0 (4607-4621).
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits the -1 return when ap_sta_add() fails with WLAN_STATUS_AP_UNABLE_TO_HANDLE_NEW_STA - right (4530-4534 then out at 4615-4618 return -1). Slice cut the head; function read in full; __check_assoc_ies, add_associated_sta and the MLE helpers not read.

name: handle_auth_cb
prose: Callback after the driver has sent (or failed to send) an authentication reply (ieee802_11.c:6363-6420; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns if the station for the destination address is not found (6371-6377). If the frame is shorter than the auth header it sets status UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE and goes to fail (6379-6385). Otherwise it reads the algorithm, transaction and status from the frame; if the frame was not acknowledged (ok == 0) it goes to fail (6388-6397). For a successful open-system reply (transaction 2) or shared-key reply (transaction 4) it sets WLAN_STA_AUTH, updates the station flags in the driver if the station was added unassociated, and returns (6399-6407). At fail it computes success_status from the frame's status code (for SAE transaction 1 through sae_status_success) and removes a station that was added unassociated from the driver, clearing added_unassoc, only when success_status is false (6410-6419). Hence an unacknowledged reply whose own status code was SUCCESS does not remove the station.
note: [R:right] reviewer: ok==0 with a successful status code leaves the added_unassoc station in the driver; the prose said it is removed - right (6392-6396 go to fail, 6411 computes success_status true, 6416 then skips the removal). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: handle_assoc_cb
prose: Callback after the driver has sent (or failed to send) an association or reassociation response (ieee802_11.c:6534-6705; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns if the station is not found (6542-6547) and, for an MLD station, if this is not the link on which the association happened (6550-6557). A frame that is too short removes the station from the driver and returns (6560-6567). It reads the status code (6569-6572). If the frame was not acknowledged it clears WLAN_STA_ASSOC_REQ_OK, removes the station from the driver when the status was success, and jumps to handle_ml (6574-6583); a non-success status also jumps to handle_ml (6586-6587). On success it stops accounting, sets WLAN_STA_ASSOC, clears WNM sleep, authorizes the station at once for open, FILS or FT cases, calls the MLME association indication, binds the VLAN (a failure jumps to handle_ml), sets the driver flags, enables a pending WDS station, sets up a WDS interface where needed, sends the WPA association event (FT or normal), calls new_assoc_sta_cb and enables the 802.1X port (6586-6669). For FILS it sets the temporal key, disconnecting the station and returning if that fails (6672-6680). If an EAPOL frame was received just before the association (pending_eapol_rx) it processes it with ieee802_1x_receive when its age is under 200 ms and frees it in either case (6683-6701). handle_ml calls hostapd_ml_handle_assoc_cb(hapd, sta, ok) (6703-6704).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: the prose claims a pending EAPOL frame younger than 200 ms is processed and freed, but the code has no such logic - wrong: it is at ieee802_11.c:6683-6701 (age.sec == 0 && age.usec < 200000 and the frees at 6698-6700). Slice cut the head; function read in full; the called helpers not read.

name: ieee802_11_sa_query_action
prose: Processes a received SA Query action frame at the AP (ieee802_11_shared.c:250-362; the packet name hostapd_sa_query_action does not exist, and the slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It ignores a frame too short to hold the transaction identifier and a group-addressed frame (260-272). When the sending station uses OCV it parses the information elements and returns on a parse failure, gets the channel info (a failure returns after a warning), derives the station's transmit parameters (a failure returns), and verifies the OCI element; a verification failure logs an OCV_FAILURE message at MSG_INFO level with the frame type and error string and returns (277-316). For an SA Query request it clears the station's post_csa_sa_query flag if the station exists and sends a response with ieee802_11_send_sa_query_resp, then returns (319-324). Any action other than request or response is ignored with a debug message (326-330). For a response it needs a station with a pending SA Query (transaction ids stored); with none, or with no matching transaction id among the stored ones, it returns (339-356); otherwise it logs that the reply to the pending query was received and stops the SA query with ap_sta_stop_sa_query (358-361).
note: [R:right] reviewer: an OCV verification failure logs at MSG_INFO, not only debug/warning - right (309: wpa_msg(..., MSG_INFO, OCV_FAILURE ...); the channel-info failure is a MSG_WARNING at 295). Real function is ieee802_11_sa_query_action; read in full (250-362); ieee802_11_send_sa_query_resp (152-247) read separately.

name: ieee802_1x_hs20_sub_rem
prose: Records that HS 2.0 subscription remediation is needed for a station (ieee802_1x.c:1753-1776; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It sets sta->remediation to 1 and frees the previous remediation_url (1755-1756). If len is greater than 2 it allocates len bytes into sta->remediation_url and returns at once if that allocation fails, in which case remediation_url has been set to NULL by the failed allocation (not left dangling) and remediation_method is not updated (1757-1760). Otherwise it stores the first byte of pos as the remediation method, copies the remaining len - 1 bytes as the URL and terminates it (1761-1763), and logs it. If len is at most 2 it sets remediation_url to NULL and logs the need without URL (1769-1774).
note: [R:right] reviewer: on malloc failure remediation_url is set to NULL, not left dangling - right (1758-1760 assigns the failed result directly to sta->remediation_url after the free at 1756). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: ieee802_1x_rekey
prose: Timer callback that rotates the default WEP broadcast key of the 802.1X authenticator (ieee802_1x.c:2256-2301; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It advances default_wep_key_idx: from 3 or more it wraps to 1 when individual WEP keys are configured (individual_wep_key_len > 0) and to 0 otherwise, else it increments it (2261-2265). It calls ieee802_1x_rekey_broadcast, which returns 0 without generating a key when default_wep_key_len is below 1 and otherwise replaces default_wep_key with random bytes; a failure of that call logs a warning, frees the key, clears the pointer and returns without rescheduling (2270-2277, and 2219-2241). It then sets the new key in the driver with hostapd_drv_set_key; a failure logs, frees the key, clears the pointer and returns without rescheduling (2281-2293). On success it notifies every station that a key is available and, when wep_rekeying_period is positive, registers the next timeout (2295-2300). In the case default_wep_key_len < 1 no new random key is generated and the driver call still runs with the existing key pointer and the configured length.
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits the default_wep_key_len < 1 path where no new random key is generated - right (ieee802_1x_rekey_broadcast returns 0 at 2223-2224, so 2270 does not fail and 2281 runs). Slice cut the head; function read in full, plus ieee802_1x_rekey_broadcast.

name: vlan_newlink
prose: Called when a VLAN network interface appears, to put it into the right bridges (vlan_full.c:461-510; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It looks for the first configured VLAN entry of hapd that is not yet configured and has the same interface name, and returns if there is none (469-476). It marks it configured and reads its description (478-482). With no VLAN description (not notempty) and a configured bridge it adds the interface to that bridge and records DVLAN_CLEAN_WLAN_PORT on success (484-488); with an untagged VLAN id within range it builds the bridge name, makes sure the bridge exists with vlan_get_bridge and adds the interface to it, recording DVLAN_CLEAN_WLAN_PORT on success (489-496). For each tagged VLAN id (stopping at the first zero) that is not the untagged id, is in range and differs from the previous one, it creates the bridge and tagged interface with vlan_newlink_tagged (498-507). Finally it always brings the interface up with ifconfig_up(ifname) (509).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: the code does not bring ifname up at the end; only the tagged-interface path may call ifconfig_up(ifname) - wrong: vlan_full.c:509 `ifconfig_up(ifname);` is the last statement of vlan_newlink and runs on every path that reaches the end (the only earlier return is 475-476). Slice cut the head; function read in full; vlan_get_bridge and br_addif not read.

name: wpa_try_alt_snonce
prose: Tries to verify a received EAPOL-Key message MIC with the earlier (alternate) SNonce of the station (wpa_auth.c:1292-1377; slice cut the head); it returns 0 when the MIC matches and the state was updated, -1 otherwise. It loops: for a PSK (non-SAE) key management it fetches the next PSK for the station with wpa_auth_get_psk and ends the loop if there is none, otherwise it uses sm->PMK; it derives a PTK with the alternate SNonce (failure ends the loop) and verifies the MIC; a match copies the PMK into sm->PMK if it came from elsewhere and sets ok (1306-1337); for non-PSK modes, or after a mismatch with a PSK, the loop continues only for PSK (1340-1342). Without a match it logs and goes to fail (1345-1349). On a match it clears alt_snonce_valid, applies a PSK VLAN id (failure goes to fail), stores FT keys when FT is in use and not completed, copies the alternate SNonce into SNonce and the derived PTK into sm->PTK, clears the local PTK with forced_memzero, sets PTK_valid and returns 0 (1352-1372). The fail label clears pmk_r0 and pmk_r1 with forced_memzero and returns -1; the local PTK is cleared only on the success path (1369) and not on the failure paths (1373-1376).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the failure path does not zero the local PTK; only pmk_r0 and pmk_r1 are zeroed - right (1369 is after the fail jump points 1348 and 1357, 1374-1375 zero only pmk_r0/pmk_r1). Slice cut the head; function read in full; wpa_derive_ptk and wpa_verify_key_mic not read.

name: __wpa_send_eapol
prose: Builds and sends one EAPOL-Key frame to a station (wpa_auth.c:1964-2180; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It computes the MIC length, the key descriptor version from the key management and cipher, and the key-data length with AES key-wrap padding when the data is encrypted (1981-2021), then allocates the frame with os_zalloc and returns silently if that fails (2023-2025). Only after that allocation does it fill the header and advance the replay counter: it shifts the stored counters, increments key_replay[0].counter, copies it into the frame and marks it valid (2049-2059). Therefore a frame allocation failure returns before the replay counter changes, while the later early returns (a failed buffer allocation at 2088 or 2098, encryption failures at 2119 and 2143, a missing valid PTK or MIC computation failure at 2154 and 2161) happen after it was advanced, so the counter is consumed without a frame being sent. When the frame is complete it increments the transmitted-frames counter, sends the frame through wpa_auth_send_eapol and frees it (2175-2179). With the MIC bit set and a valid PTK it computes the MIC, and for a group frame the test option can corrupt it (2148-2173).
note: [R:right] reviewer: claims it always advances key_replay, but a frame allocation failure returns before the advancement - right (2023-2025 return before 2049-2059). Partly read: head (1964-2060), tail (2140-2180) and a grep of the middle (2060-2140: nonce, RSC, key-data encryption with AES wrap or RC4 handled in lines 2088-2143 by their returns only).

name: SM_STATE(WPA_PTK, PTKCALCNEGOTIATING)
prose: Generated state-machine function for the PTKCALCNEGOTIATING state of the WPA authenticator's 4-Way Handshake (macro invocation SM_STATE(WPA_PTK, PTKCALCNEGOTIATING) at wpa_auth.c:3626; the packet name wpa_ptk_PTKCALCNEGOTIATING_step does not exist); it returns nothing. It enters the state (SM_ENTRY_MA), clears EAPOLKeyReceived and update_snonce, and tries to verify message 2/4 (3649-3652). In a loop it picks a PMK: for PSK key management (not SAE) the next PSK found by wpa_auth_get_psk (no PSK ends the loop), otherwise sm->PMK or the PMKSA's key (3662-3686); it derives a PTK with the stored SNonce (failure ends the loop) and verifies the MIC of the last received EAPOL-Key (or AEAD decrypts it when there is no MIC) (3690-3713). On a successful MIC check it copies the used PMK into sm->PMK immediately, before the later checks, so a later failure leaves sm->PMK changed (3695-3704). On a mismatch it retries with the OWE SHA-256 workaround, then without the KDK, and for PSK continues with the next PSK (3717-3740). If nothing matched and a RADIUS PSK request is possible it requests it, sets waiting_radius_psk and leaves via out (3751-3762); otherwise it logs an invalid MIC, reports a PSK failure when a PSK was found, and goes to out (3764-3770). The remaining part checks the key data, RSN elements, FT and other conditions and disconnects the station with wpa_sta_disconnect on mismatches, going to out in each case (goto out at 3785-3953, disconnects at 3848, 3864, 3912, 3951, 3959).
note: [R:right] reviewer: sm->PMK is updated as soon as the MIC verifies, not only on full success; later failures leave it changed - right (3699-3702 versus the later gotos). Partly read: head (3626-3770) line by line; the rest (3771-3960: key data and RSN IE comparison, FT checks, PTK installation) was scanned only for goto and disconnect lines.

name: wpa_ft_process_auth_req
prose: Processes the Fast BSS Transition (FT) authentication request elements of a station on the AP (wpa_auth_ft.c:3168-3442; slice cut the head); it returns WLAN_STATUS_SUCCESS (0), a WLAN_STATUS_* failure code, or -1 when the PMK-R1 must be pulled from the R0KH asynchronously. It clears *resp_ies and the length and pmk_r1_name_valid (3187-3190) and returns UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE at once if the elements cannot be parsed (3196-3198). From there on it returns through out: INVALID_MDIE for a missing or mismatching mobility-domain element, INVALID_FTIE for a missing FT element or R0KH-ID, INVALID_PMKID for a missing PMKID (3201-3232); failures of wpa_ft_set_key_mgmt, random generation, PTK derivation and of the VLAN, identity and CUI setters leave the initial UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE (3234-3235, 3317-3320, 3372-3376, 3392-3402). It derives the PMK-R1 name and finds the PMK-R1: locally generated for FT-PSK when ft_psk_generate_local is set (a failure there gives INVALID_PMKID), else from the local cache for the allowed hash lengths, else derived from a local PMK-R0, else it asks the R0KH with wpa_ft_pull_pmk_r1: a failure of the pull gives INVALID_PMKID, and success sets the result to -1 (pending) and leaves (3240-3308). With a PMK-R1 it stores it, generates the ANonce, takes the SNonce from the FT element according to the key length (INVALID_FTIE if it is too short), derives the PTK (with a KDK when configured) and installs it, then builds the response RSN, mobility-domain and FT elements into a new buffer (3310-3430). On a build failure it frees the buffer (the pointer is not reset) with the result still UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE (3436-3437); on success it returns WLAN_STATUS_SUCCESS (3434-3441). There is no INVALID_RSNIE return in this function.
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: omits the WLAN_STATUS_INVALID_RSNIE return when the RSNIE is missing - wrong for this function: there is no such return (wpa_auth_ft.c:3168-3442 uses INVALID_MDIE, INVALID_FTIE and INVALID_PMKID); the missing-PMKID check is at 3228-3231. Slice cut the head; function read in full; the FT helper functions not read.

name: wpa_validate_wpa_ie
prose: Validates the WPA or RSN information element of a station's association request and stores state on sm (wpa_auth_ie.c:613-1105; slice cut the head); it returns a WPA_* result, WPA_IE_OK on success. It returns WPA_NOT_ENABLED if wpa_auth or sm is NULL (628-629) and WPA_INVALID_IE for a missing or empty element (631-632). It parses the element and rejects an unsupported protocol version (WPA_INVALID_PROTO), a malformed element, an invalid group cipher (WPA_INVALID_GROUP), an AKM not allowed (WPA_INVALID_AKMP), a disallowed pairwise cipher (WPA_INVALID_PAIRWISE), management-frame-protection violations (WPA_MGMT_FRAME_PROTECTION_VIOLATION, WPA_INVALID_MGMT_GROUP_CIPHER), an invalid mobility-domain element when FT is used (WPA_INVALID_MDIE) and PMKID mismatches (WPA_INVALID_PMKID), plus WPA_DENIED_OTHER_REASON for other denied cases (the returns at lines 629-1059, listed by line in the source). On success it records the selected key management, ciphers and extended-key-id state in sm, copies the element into sm->wpa_ie (WPA_ALLOC_FAIL if the allocation fails) and stores or clears the RSNXE copy in sm->rsnxe (WPA_ALLOC_FAIL if that allocation fails), and returns WPA_IE_OK (1063-1104). The function has no WPA_INVALID_RSXE or WPA_INVALID_OWE_DH return: rsnxe is only copied at 1089-1100 and owe_dh does not appear in the body.
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: omits possible WPA_INVALID_RSXE and WPA_INVALID_OWE_DH return codes from rsnxe/owe_dh validation - wrong: the returns of the function (listed by a grep, 629-1104) do not include those codes, and rsnxe and owe_dh are not validated here. Partly read: head (613-632), the return list and the tail (1060-1104); the middle (633-1060: version, cipher and AKM selection, MFP, FT and PMKID checks) was scanned only by its return statements.
